topics.label: Introduction to cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecture topic and outlines the intended learning outcomes for comparing cancer treatments.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional modalities of cancer treatment, including surgical resection, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapeutics alongside their mechanisms, toxicities, and resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Targeted therapies exploiting intrinsic cellular vulnerabilities and genetic defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain therapeutic strategies designed to exploit specific cancer vulnerabilities, including hormone dependency, cell cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and defective DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitors, oncogene addiction, and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the targeting of hyperactivated oncogenic kinases with small-molecule inhibitors and detail the mechanisms through which tumors develop resistance or drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the use of engineered antibodies to target cell surface receptors and selectively deliver cytotoxic payloads to cancer cells.

topics.label: Cancer immune surveillance and immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate the role of the immune system in recognizing tumors and examine modern immunotherapeutic strategies including checkpoint inhibitors, BiTEs, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Clinical challenges, historical trends, and future directions in cancer management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate broader perspectives on cancer management, covering therapeutic challenges, genomic stratification, historical survival trends, and future ethical considerations.
